properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be

* WHERE...Portions of north central and northeast New Mexico,

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A near-record to record surge of moisture combined with a storm
system moving across northern New Mexico will continue to bring

burn scar.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 30 at 1:08AM CDT until October 1 at 6:00PM CDT by NWS Topeka KS
properties.description:
* WHAT...Multiple rounds of heavy rain with an increasing potential
for flooding.

* WHERE...Portions of north central and northeast Kansas, including
the following counties, in north central Kansas, Clay, Cloud,
Ottawa, Republic and Washington. In northeast Kansas, Brown,
Jackson, Marshall, Nemaha, Pottawatomie and Riley.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A slow moving, moisture laden system is expected to bring
widespread rainfall of two to four inches, with locally higher
amounts of around six inches.
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH THURSDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Harrison; Shelby; Pottawattamie; Mills; Montgomery; Fremont; Page; Dodge; Washington; Butler; Saunders; Douglas; Sarpy; Seward; Lancaster; Cass; Otoe; Saline; Jefferson; Gage; Johnson; Nemaha; Pawnee; Richardson
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 30 at 12:46AM CDT until October 1 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Omaha/Valley NE
properties.description:
Heavy rain will spread across the area today and into Thursday
morning. This rain will be focused along and south of the Platte
River and into southwest Iowa. While this rain is spread out over a
longer period of time, flash flooding cannot be ruled out. The flash
flooding threat is highest this afternoon and evening.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Iowa, including the following
counties, Fremont, Harrison, Mills, Montgomery, Page, Pottawattamie
and Shelby and Nebraska, including the following counties, Butler,
Cass, Dodge, Douglas, Gage, Jefferson, Johnson, Lancaster, Nemaha,
Otoe, Pawnee, Richardson, Saline, Sarpy, Saunders, Seward and
Washington.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Area creeks and streams are running high and could flood with more
heavy rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Prolonged rain falling on saturated soil could lead to flooding
in the coming days. Rainfall amounts of 2-4 inches are expected
in many locations through Thursday, with localized amounts
topping 5 to 6 inches for some.
- For flood safety information, visit weather.gov/safety/flood.
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH WEDNESDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Northwestern San Juan Mountains; Southwest San Juan Mountains; San Juan River Basin
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 29 at 10:07PM MDT until October 1 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of Colorado, including the following areas, Animas
River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, Northwest San Juan
Mountains, Paradox Valley/Lower Dolores River, San Juan River
Basin, Southwest San Juan Mountains and Uncompahgre Plateau and
Dallas Divide and southeast Utah, including the following areas,
Canyonlands/Natural Bridges, La Sal and Abajo Mountains and
Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...Through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Flooding will be possible over burn scars, at low-water
crossings, and along creeks, streams, washes, arroyos and other
flood-prone locations. Creeks and streams may rise out of their
banks. Unpaved roads could become muddy and impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Periods of heavy rainfall, associated with remnant moisture from
Hurricane Polo, are expected to produce numerous showers and
embedded thunderstorms. Heavy rain falling on saturated soils and
burn scars could lead to localized flash flooding and rises on
local rivers. Rainfall is expected to end by late Wednesday, but
rivers may rise out of their banks overnight Wednesday even after
rainfall has ended.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 29 at 9:54PM CDT until October 1 at 3:00PM CDT by NWS Quad Cities IA IL
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Quad Cities has issued a Flood
Watch for the following rivers in Iowa...

English River at Kalona affecting Johnson and Washington Counties.

North Skunk River near Sigourney affecting Keokuk County.

* WHAT...Flooding is possible.

* WHERE...North Skunk River near Sigourney.

* WHEN...From Thursday morning to Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Water affects most agricultural land near
Sigourney.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 PM CDT Tuesday the stage was 11.3 feet.
- Forecast...Flood stage may be reached Thursday morning.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you are in the watch area, remain alert to possible flooding.

Residents and those with interests near the river should monitor
rising water levels and be prepared for possible Flood Warnings.

The next statement will be issued by Wednesday evening.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH IN EFFECT FROM THURSDAY MORNING TO THURSDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Llano; Burnet; Williamson; Val Verde; Edwards; Real; Kerr; Bandera; Gillespie; Kendall; Blanco; Hays; Travis; Bastrop; Kinney; Uvalde; Medina; Bexar; Comal; Guadalupe; Caldwell; Maverick; Zavala; Frio; Atascosa; Wilson; Gonzales; Dimmit
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 29 at 5:47PM CDT until October 2 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
The weather pattern on Wednesday will begin to change as an
approaching upper level low over the southwestern U.S. weakens the
subtropical ridge axis over Texas and the western Gulf. Isolated to
scattered showers and thunderstorms will develop during the daytime
hours. A Pacific cold front will move into the region Thursday
spreading showers and thunderstorms over more of the area. Rainfall
totals from Wednesday evening through Friday will be 2-4 inches with
isolated amounts up to 8 inches possible.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Texas, including the following
counties, Atascosa, Bandera, Bastrop, Bexar, Blanco, Burnet,
Caldwell, Comal, Dimmit, Edwards, Frio, Gillespie, Gonzales,
Guadalupe, Hays, Kendall, Kerr, Kinney, Llano, Maverick, Medina,
Real, Travis, Uvalde, Val Verde, Williamson, Wilson and Zavala.

* WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...There is a potential for life threatening flooding
somewhere in the watch area. Excessive runoff may result in
flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Creeks and streams may rise out of their
banks. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.
Low-water crossings may be flooded. Extensive street flooding and
flooding of creeks and rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rainfall totals of 2-4 inches with isolated amounts of 8 inches
are possible.
-  Some locations that may experience flooding include...
San Antonio, Austin, Round Rock, New Braunfels, Cedar Park,
Georgetown, San Marcos, Pflugerville, Medina, Schertz, Kyle, Del
Rio, Eagle Pass, Seguin, Cibolo, Kerrville, Converse, Universal
City, Taylor and Uvalde.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM WEDNESDAY EVENING THROUGH FRIDAY EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Southeast Elbert County Below 6000 Feet/South Lincoln County
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 29 at 2:05PM MDT until October 1 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Far southeastern Elbert and southern Lincoln county.

* WHEN...From midnight MDT tonight through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A surge of tropical moisture from the remnants of Hurricane Polo
and a storm system will bring a threat of flooding late tonight
through Thursday morning. Periods of heavy rainfall may lead to
totals of 1 to 2.5 inches in the watch area, with locally higher
amounts possible.
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.
